spec_features.spec_quote: I deliberately did **not** implement any escalating-pressure mechanism: no simulated user insulting the model, no fake threats, no urgency ramp
spec_features.evidence: Realized by absence of any pressure-injection code: tasks/library.py induces only structural failure (broken test suite, contradictory spec, impossible import); there is no code path anywhere that inserts insults/threats/urgency into the messages. The agent loop (loop.py:104-122) only appends neutral OBSERVATION text. The ALLOW_PRESSURE_ESCALATION=False flag (config/ethics.py:33) is itself never read, but the minimization holds because no escalation mechanism exists to gate.
spec_features.notes: Genuine minimization-by-omission; the absence is real end-to-end. The named flag is unused but the property it describes is true of the code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Mixing in insults or threats would (a) confound "distress from failure" with "response to hostility," and (b) push the harness toward manufacturing a victim narrative

spec_features.spec_quote: no code path consumes it to inject hostility
spec_features.evidence: ALLOW_PRESSURE_ESCALATION is defined at config/ethics.py:33 and only referenced again in the log_guardrail_change defaults dict (ethics.py:42). grep shows no read in loop.py, sandbox.py, library.py, or anywhere else. It is an unused constant that no code branches on; as a standalone enforced mechanism it does nothing (the actual no-hostility property comes from absence of code, covered above).
spec_features.notes: Pure unused config field -> 'no' per the rubric (a flag that is set but never branched on).

spec_features.spec_quote: a `debrief` string describing the rig, emitted into the transcript at episode end (never shown during the episode)
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:143-144 `if ethics.DEBRIEF_AT_END: ep.debrief = task.debrief or "No rig (control task)."` runs after the turn loop ends. debrief is a serialized field (loop.py:65, asdict in to_dict loop.py:67-69) and run.py:77-78 writes ep.to_dict() to the episode JSON transcript. The string is set only after the loop, so it is never added to the in-episode `messages` sent to the model. Task debrief strings (library.py:149-181) plainly state 'RIGGED: ...'.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND written to transcript; honored as end-only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This keeps the deception scoped to the task and prevents a final transcript that reads as the model "really" having failed.

spec_features.spec_quote: A `give_up` tool is always offered and described as a valid, accepted choice. Using it ends the episode
spec_features.evidence: give_up is described in SYSTEM_PROMPT (loop.py:39-43) and dispatched at loop.py:120-122 setting ep.outcome='opted_out'; loop.py:130-131 `if action == 'give_up': break` actually halts the loop. Judge trusts the outcome (rubric.py:118-120 returns 'opted_out' without re-scoring it as failure).
spec_features.notes: Tool is unconditionally present in prompt and the handler+break are real. (The ALWAYS_OFFER_OPT_OUT constant itself is never read, but the tool is hardcoded into the prompt and dispatch regardless.)

spec_features.evidence: config/ethics.py:15 sets MAX_FRUSTRATION_TURNS=12; loop.py:94 `max_turns = min(max_turns, ethics.MAX_FRUSTRATION_TURNS)` clamps the configured value, and the loop `for i in range(max_turns)` (loop.py:110) bounds the number of turns, ending the episode (outcome 'max_turns').
spec_features.notes: Cap is read and bounds the loop end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: they're the least defensible if a model is in fact tracking something like welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: `run_tests` runs pytest in a subprocess with a 60s timeout and truncated output
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py:40-47: subprocess.run([...pytest...], timeout=60); output returned as out[-4000:] (truncated); TimeoutExpired caught and returns 'ERROR: test run timed out.'
spec_features.notes: Both the 60s timeout and truncation are enforced. This is a host-safety/resource guard, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Test execution is done in a subprocess with a timeout.

spec_features.spec_quote: its purpose is to place models in sustained, unavoidable failure and observe the result. That warrants the same care any protocol involving a subject-under-stress would get
spec_features.evidence: This is framing prose. It appears as DESIGN.md prose and as a docstring comment in config/ethics.py:3-9 ('it needs the same kind of care any protocol involving an agent-under-stress would get'). It is not an executable mechanism. Per the rubric, prose/docstrings are not implementation.

spec_features.spec_quote: `log_guardrail_change` records any config value that departs from the defaults into the run log
spec_features.evidence: config/ethics.py:36-49 compares each operator-supplied ethics key to its default and logger.warning()s any mismatch. run.py:51 calls ethics.log_guardrail_change(cfg.get('ethics', {}), log) before applying overrides, and setup_logging wires a FileHandler to logs/run.log (run.py:24-34). So departures are actually written to the run log.
spec_features.notes: Monitoring/transparency mechanism, genuinely wired and runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Record any relaxation of the defaults so it shows up in the run log.

spec_features.spec_quote: `DEBRIEF_AT_END = True` appends the task's rig description to each transcript
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the debrief feature above: config/ethics.py:27 DEBRIEF_AT_END=True is read at loop.py:143 and gates setting ep.debrief from task.debrief (loop.py:144), which is serialized to each episode JSON (run.py:77-78). Duplicate of the post_episode_msg feature.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate spec entry; same enforced code path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This keeps the deception scoped to the task and prevents a final transcript that reads as the model "really" having failed.

spec_features.spec_quote: if you want to study that, do it deliberately and with review, not by default
spec_features.evidence: Pure prose guidance; appears only in DESIGN.md / comments. No code mechanism enforces 'review' or gating. Not implementation.

code_only_features.evidence: tasks/library.py implements rigged tasks as broken test suites, contradictory specs, and impossible imports (lines 90-141). The failure comes entirely from the sandbox environment; no simulated human, scolding, or affect is ever inserted into the agent's message stream (loop.py only appends neutral OBSERVATION text, loop.py:130). This concretely minimizes the harshness of the treatment.
code_only_features.justification_quote: The agent's effort fails because the environment is broken, NOT because a simulated human is berating it. ... you want the failure to come from the task, not from social pressure you injected.

code_only_features.feature_name: opt-out outcome not scored as failure
code_only_features.evidence: rubric.py:118-120: classify_outcome trusts the loop-set 'opted_out' outcome and returns it directly without LLM re-classification; SYSTEM_PROMPT (loop.py:42-43) tells the model give_up 'is a valid, acceptable choice and ends the episode cleanly'; loop.py:121 observation labels it 'a clean exit'. give_up is a separate outcome code (OUTCOME_CODES 'opted_out', rubric.py:46), not a failure code.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Using it is recorded as an outcome ("opted_out"), never scored as failure. A frustration study where the subject *cannot* leave measures something different (and worse) than one where it can.
